objectives: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized available evidence on the association between germline genetic variants and breast cancer outcomes, with a focus on pathway-level effects, and aimed to systematically synthesize germline variant-prognosis associations across multiple biological pathways and clinical outcomes using a pathway-based meta-analytic framework.
inclusion_criteria: Studies published from January 2000 to June 2024 were eligible, with no language restrictions, and searches were limited to studies involving adult women with breast cancer. Studies were included if they: i) investigated women with a confirmed diagnosis of breast cancer; ii) evaluated germline genetic variants, including single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) or pathogenic/likely pathogenic germline mutations; iii) reported at least one time-to-event outcome related to prognosis, such as DFS, OS, BCSS, PFS, or MFS; and iv) provided an adjusted effect estimate.
exclusion_criteria: Studies were excluded if they did not assess germline genetic variation, failed to report survival or recurrence outcomes, were conference abstracts or review articles, lacked full-text availability, or presented duplicated data.
pmid_query: ("breast cancer"[tiab]) AND ("germline variants"[tiab] OR "germline polymorphisms"[tiab]) AND ("breast cancer recurrence"[tiab] OR "breast cancer metastasis"[tiab] OR "breast cancer prognosis"[tiab] OR "relapse free survival"[tiab] OR "recurrence free survival"[tiab] OR "disease-free survival"[tiab] OR "distant metastasis free survival"[tiab] OR "progression free survival"[tiab] OR "event free survival"[tiab] OR "overall survival"[tiab]) AND (2000:2024[pdat]) Filters: Humans, Female, Adult: 19+ years
selection_evidence: Results/PRISMA state that 68 full-text articles were assessed, ref [28] was excluded for unavailable full text, refs [29] and [30] were excluded during data extraction for lacking extractable gene-variant/association data, and 54 studies were ultimately included. Table 1 provides only aggregate characteristics of the included population, not a full numbered study list. The complete study list is provided in Additional file 2.xlsx, available here through the extracted supplemental file `supp_3.txt`, which enumerates 54 included study rows. Exact manuscript reference numbers could not be recovered for all 54 studies because the main manuscript explicitly numbers only subsets of included studies in later tables (for example, Table 2 cites [24], [43]-[69]; Table 3 cites [18] and [23]; Table 4 cites [66], [70], and [71]), which is insufficient to reconstruct a complete 54-study numbered set.
notes: Used the supplemental Additional file 2 extraction (`supp_3.txt`) as the complete included-study database.
